summary: Background warmup IO surge causing GPU attach failures and unexpected dedicated pool thinning
description:
Issue summary:
A dedicated customer (VerdantAI) in us-west-2 reported a sustained throughput degradation beginning 2026-03-14 10:20 UTC after onboarding additional batch workers. Symptoms: elevated GPU attach timeouts, rising 429s on reserved routes, and gradual dedicated pool thinning (visible as reduced attached GPU slots per host).

Impact:
- Customer reports 40-60% increase in p99 latency and repeated timeouts for short-batched requests.
- Autoscaler did not open new hosts quickly; several allocation attempts timed out leading to fallbacks to lower-tier capacity.
- Visible disruption for multiple models; downstream request retries increased.

Environment:
- prod, region us-west-2, dedicated pool "verdant-dedicated-01"
- Redwood serving runtime v3.4.1, allocator v2.9.0, nvme-snapshotter v1.3.0

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Customer ramped 200 small batch workers (100-200 token short requests) between 10:15-10:25 UTC.
2) Within minutes, NVMe IO for snapshotter spiked (sustained 3x baseline) and host-level IO wait increased.
3) GPU attach loop began to surface ASYNC_ATTACH_TIMEOUT errors and attach retries increased.
4) Autoscaler saw perceived low attach success rate and began leaving slots free (thin view) instead of scaling up.

Observed behaviour:
- Metrics: attach_latency.p50 went from 45ms to 320ms, attach_latency.p99 > 2s.
- Kernel logs show repeated "attach: NVME_IO_WAIT" and "cuda-context-attach-timeout" between hosts 10.0.12.*.
- nvme-snapshotter logs contain frequent small-file flush storms from customer sidecar during warmup.
- Dedicated pool slot count decreased by ~18% across the shard over 10 minutes.

Expected behaviour:
- Short-burst warmups should not cause sustained NVMe IO amplification or block attachment; autoscaler should add capacity when attach success falls below threshold.

Relevant links/metrics:
- Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/dedicated/attach-latency?region=us-west-2&pool=verdant-dedicated-01
- Pager view: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/SUP-550501
- Sample logs: s3://redwood-logs/verdant/sup-550501/host-10.0.12.45-attach.log

Initial ask:
- Triage root cause and provide mitigation so VerdantAI can complete onboarding without rolling back to self-serve routes.
- If rollback not possible quickly, provide recommended workaround and ETA for fix.
comments: 2026-03-14 10:42 UTC - Aisha Patel: Customer reports p99 latency spike and 500/504s when calling reserved route. They attached temporary debug logs to ticket.
2026-03-14 11:05 UTC - Miguel Torres: Acknowledged. Reproduced attach_timeout on a staging repro; beginning collection of nvme and host metrics. Adding SRE on-call.

2026-03-14 11:20 UTC - SRE Oncall (Elena Kwon): Seeing sustained iowait and snapshotter small-file write spikes coincident with customer's warmup. Marking as potential noisy neighbor IO amplification.
2026-03-14 12:00 UTC - Miguel Torres: Pushed temporary autoscaler threshold bypass for verdant-dedicated-01 to allow scale-up despite attach failures (risk: transient oversubscription). Monitoring.

2026-03-14 13:10 UTC - Customer (VerdantAI, engineer Tom Lin): Confirmed partial recovery of throughput after autoscaler override; however customer still sees intermittent short-batch timeouts and wants root cause.
2026-03-15 09:00 UTC - Miguel Torres: Investigations continue; filing follow-up actions. Assigned to allocator and snapshotter teams for deeper analysis.
investigation_notes: Host-level blk_iostats show 3x baseline write amplification from snapshotter processes during 10:15-10:30 UTC.
Snapshotter configuration includes frequent per-session metadata flushes for short-lived sessions; this pattern amplifies IO for many small batches.
Attach path waits on NVMe acknowledgements; increased iowait correlates with attach latency and timeouts.
Autoscaler currently uses attach_success_rate heuristic to decide scale; low attach_success caused autoscaler to back off instead of joining more hosts (hysteresis observed).
No reproducible kernel regressions in serving runtime; root appears to be I/O amplification from snapshotter + autoscaler hysteresis.
Customer sidecar library (verdant-sidecar v0.8.2) appears to flush small checkpoints frequently during warmup; reached out to customer's eng for sidecar config dump.
resolution: Mitigation applied: temporarily overridden autoscaler attach_success_rate threshold for verdant-dedicated-01 to force scale-up while we fix IO pattern.

Workaround recommended to customer: set sidecar 'checkpoint.batch_flush' to false and use aggregated flush interval (provided config snippet) while onboarding, or stagger worker ramp-up by 5s windows.

Longer-term fixes: allocator team to add short-term backstop that allows growth when attach latency rises but attach failures are transient; snapshotter team to implement small-file coalescing in v1.3.1.
Follow-ups: create postmortem runbook, update dedicated autoscaler heuristics, and coordinate a joint rollout with VerdantAI to validate sidecar change.
